'''Ryan Anthony Gomes''' (born September 1, 1982) is an American [[college basketball]] coach and former professional player who last served as an assistant coach for the [[Providence Friars]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Ryan Gomes Named Men's Basketball Assistant Coach|url=https://friars.com/news/2025/6/2/mens-basketball-ryan-gomes-named-mens-basketball-assistant-coach|access-date=June 3, 2025|website=Friars.com}}</ref> He was named a First Team All-American [[Power forward (basketball)|power forward]] at [[Providence Friars men's basketball|Providence College]] before being selected with the 50th overall pick in the [[2005 NBA draft]] by the [[Boston Celtics]].

==High school career==
Gomes attended Wilby High School, where he was the captain of the basketball team during his final two seasons, averaging 26.9 points, 16 rebounds, 5.0 assists and 3.0 blocks per game. Gomes was awarded the Billy Finn Award as the top player in Waterbury, as well as being named [[Naugatuck Valley League]] MVP. During his high school days, Gomes also pitched on his baseball team where he recorded a .013 ERA. He received collegiate scholarship offers from [[Vanderbilt University|Vanderbilt]], Florida and LSU but ultimately chose to attend [[Providence College]].<ref name="bio">{{cite web|url=http://www.friars.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/gomes_ryan00.html|title=Ryan Gomes bio|work=Friars.com|access-date=January 7, 2016|archive-date=July 5, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150705214121/http://www.friars.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/gomes_ryan00.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==College career==
Gomes played his college career for [[Providence Friars men's basketball|Providence]] averaging 18.4 points, 8.9 rebounds, 2.3 assists and 1.6 steals in 35.1 minutes in his four years with the Friars. He had his best year as a junior, tallying 18.9 points, 9.4 rebounds, 2.3 assists and 1.6 steals per game which earned him a Consensus First Team All-American.<ref name="bio" /><ref name="D-Fenders">{{cite web|url=http://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/?id=5087222|title=D-Fenders Acquire Ryan Gomes|work=OurSportsCentral.com|date=January 7, 2016|access-date=January 7, 2016}}</ref>

==Professional career==

=== Boston Celtics (2005–2007) ===

====2005–06 season====
Wearing number 4, Gomes was expected to play off the bench in his [[rookie]] season spelling Celtics star [[Paul Pierce]]. His playing time and statistical impact were limited early in the season. However, on January 26, 2006, the Celtics executed a multiplayer trade with the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] that freed up roster space for Gomes to play. Soon after that, fellow Celtic [[Kendrick Perkins]] was injured and Gomes was inserted in the starting line-up.

After becoming a starter, Gomes excelled, and kept his job even after Perkins returned. On February 24, 2006, he collected 17 rebounds and scored 13 points in a win over the [[Portland Trail Blazers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://sports.espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=260224022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121025163310/http://sports.espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=260224022|url-status=dead|archive-date=October 25, 2012|title=Pierce pours in 37 in Celtics' win over Portland|publisher=ESPN|date=February 25, 2006|access-date=February 25, 2006}}</ref> Gomes scored at least 10 points in 21 of the 29 games he started in 2006, and in 7 of those games he also had a [[Double (basketball)#Double-double|double-double]]. The second half of his rookie season was a definite success.

Gomes was named to NBA All-Rookie Second Team for the [[2005–06 NBA season|2005–06 season]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/celtics/news/press050406-gomes-rookie-team.html |title=Gomes Named to NBA All-Rookie Second Team |work=NBA.com |date=May 4, 2006 |access-date=May 4, 2006 |url-status=unfit |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090309090212/http://www.nba.com/celtics/news/press050406-gomes-rookie-team.html |archive-date=March 9, 2009 }}</ref> and chose to play in the Celtics' 2006 NBA summer-league team. Gomes was named to the summer league all-first team for the second consecutive year.

====2006–07 season====
Gomes continued to make a significant impact starting 60 games for the Celtics in the 2006–07 season. Gomes averaged more than 30 minutes played, scoring 12.1 points per game, along with 1.6 [[assist (basketball)|assists]] and 5.6 [[Rebound (basketball)|rebounds]]. On November 8, 2006, Gomes recorded his first career [[triple-double]] collecting 10 points, 12 rebounds, and a career-high 10 assists against the [[Charlotte Bobcats]] in the Celtics' first win of the 2006–07 season after an 0–3 start.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://sports.espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=261108002|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121023134657/http://sports.espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=261108002|url-status=dead|archive-date=October 23, 2012|title=West's OT jumper gives Celtics first win on season|publisher=ESPN|date=November 9, 2006|access-date=November 9, 2006}}</ref> On January 20, Gomes scored a career-high 31 points in a January 20, 2007 [[Overtime (sports)|overtime]] loss to the [[Washington Wizards]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://sports.espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=270120027|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070124023605/http://sports.espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=270120027|url-status=dead|archive-date=January 24, 2007|title=Jamison shrugs off sore knee in time for Wiz to stave off Celtics|publisher=ESPN|date=January 24, 2007|access-date=January 24, 2007}}</ref> Coming off the bench on March 4, Gomes tied his career-high of 17 rebounds and scored 21 points while playing a total of 52 minutes in a double overtime victory against the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://sports.espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=270304002|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070307075356/http://sports.espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=270304002|url-status=dead|archive-date=March 7, 2007|title=West scores 31 after halftime in Celtics' 2OT win|publisher=ESPN|date=March 4, 2007|access-date=March 4, 2007}}</ref>

On March 7, Gomes sprained his left foot and did not play in the second half of the game against the [[Houston Rockets]]. He sat out the following 7 games, and returned to the Celtics' roster playing limited minutes beginning on March 21. Near the end of the season, Gomes began regularly shooting [[Three-point field goal|three-point shots]], making 14 of 34 in April, after shooting only 5 for 17 in his career to that point.

Gomes attracted the attention of the national media for comments he made following a Celtics' loss to the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] on April 13. Neither Gomes nor starting [[point guard]] [[Rajon Rondo]] played in the game's final, decisive minutes. After, Gomes said, "I probably (would have played), but since we were in the hunt for a high draft pick, of course things are different." This was the first public comment by a Celtic in 2007 implying that the team was losing games purposely, to improve their status for the [[2007 NBA draft]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://scores.espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=270413002|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070906013720/http://scores.espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=270413002|url-status=dead|archive-date=September 6, 2007|title=Boston loses sixth straight to clinch 2nd-worst record in NBA|publisher=ESPN|date=April 13, 2007|access-date=April 13, 2007}}</ref>

=== Minnesota Timberwolves (2007–2010) ===
[[File:Gomes at Seeds of Peace.JPG|thumb|right|Gomes visiting [[Seeds of Peace]] in July 2007]]
On July 31, 2007, Gomes was traded along with [[Gerald Green]], [[Al Jefferson]], [[Theo Ratliff]], [[Sebastian Telfair]], and draft picks, to the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] for [[Kevin Garnett]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Mark |last=Murphy |url=http://celtics.bostonherald.com/celtics/view.bg?articleid=1014449 |title=Garnett deal finalized |work=BostonHerald.com |date=July 31, 2007 |access-date=July 31, 2007 |url-status=unfit |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070818092445/http://celtics.bostonherald.com/celtics/view.bg?articleid=1014449 |archive-date=August 18, 2007 }}</ref> On January 21, 2008, Gomes scored a career high 35 points against the [[Golden State Warriors]] in a 109–108 win.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.covers.com/pageLoader/pageLoader.aspx?page=/data/nba/results/2007-2008/recap754264.html|title=Garnett deal finalized|work=Covers.com|date=January 21, 2008|access-date=January 21, 2008}}</ref> Gomes played in all 82 Timberwolves games in 2007–08, starting 74 of them, and he averaged 12.6 points, 5.8 rebounds, and 1.8 assists per game.

Gomes also played in all 82 games in the 2008–09 season in which he set a career high in points scored per game (13.3).

On June 24, 2010, Gomes was traded to the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] with the draft rights to [[Luke Babbitt]] for [[Martell Webster]]. Gomes was waived by Portland on June 29, 2010.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=5341016|title=Blazers waive forward Gomes|publisher=ESPN|date=June 29, 2010|access-date=June 29, 2010}}</ref>

=== Los Angeles Clippers (2010–2012) ===
On July 8, 2010, Gomes was signed by the Clippers.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/clippers/news/breakingnews_gomes_100708.html|title=CLIPPERS SIGN FREE AGENT FORWARD RYAN GOMES|work=NBA.com|date=July 8, 2010|access-date=July 9, 2010}}</ref> He was waived by the team on July 17, 2012, via the [[amnesty clause]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/clippers/news/clippers-waive-ryan-gomes|title=CLIPPERS WAIVE RYAN GOMES|work=NBA.com|date=July 17, 2012|access-date=July 17, 2012}}</ref>

=== Artland Dragons (2012–2013) ===
On November 22, 2012, Gomes signed with the [[Artland Dragons]] of Germany's [[Basketball Bundesliga]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Mike |last=McDermott |url=http://news.providencejournal.com/sports/college/2012/11/ryan-gomes-to-play-in-germany.html |title=Ryan Gomes to play in Germany |work=[[Providence Journal]] |date=November 22, 2012 |access-date=November 25, 2012 |url-status=unfit |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121201213322/http://news.providencejournal.com/sports/college/2012/11/ryan-gomes-to-play-in-germany.html |archive-date=December 1, 2012 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.artland-dragons.de/saison/news/news-detail/article/dragons-holen-gomes-aus-der-nba.html|title=Dragons holen Gomes aus der NBA|work=Artland-Dragons.de|date=November 22, 2012|access-date=November 25, 2012|language=de}}</ref>

=== Oklahoma City Thunder (2013–2014) ===
On August 7, 2013, Gomes signed with the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/thunder/news/gomes_130807|title=Thunder Signs Ryan Gomes|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=August 7, 2013|access-date=August 7, 2013}}</ref>

On January 7, 2014, a three-team trade was completed between the Thunder, the [[Boston Celtics]], and the [[Memphis Grizzlies]]. Oklahoma City traded Gomes to Boston in exchange for second round draft picks in 2014 and 2017 from the Grizzlies; he was subsequently waived by the Celtics. As part of the transaction, the Grizzlies also traded [[Jerryd Bayless]] to the Celtics in exchange for [[Courtney Lee]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/thunder/news/thunder-acquires-two-second-round-draft-picks|title=Thunder Acquires Two Second-Round Draft Picks|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=January 7, 2014|access-date=January 8, 2014}}</ref>

===Laboral Kutxa (2014)===
On September 11, 2014, Gomes signed with [[Saski Baskonia|Laboral Kutxa]] of Spain.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/spain/134428/ryan-gomes-signs-with-laboral-kutxa.html|title=Ryan Gomes signs with Laboral Kutxa|work=Sportando.com|date=September 11, 2014|access-date=September 11, 2014}}</ref> On October 27, 2014, he parted ways with Laboral Kutxa, after playing only one game in the ACB League.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/spain/139039/ryan-gomes-and-laboral-kutxa-part-ways.html|title=Ryan Gomes and Laboral Kutxa part ways|work=Sportando.com|date=October 27, 2014|access-date=October 27, 2014}}</ref>

===Los Angeles D-Fenders (2016)===
On January 7, 2016, Gomes was acquired by the [[Los Angeles D-Fenders]] of the [[NBA Development League]].<ref name="D-Fenders" /> Over the course of the 2015–16 season, he scored in double figures 28 times, including two 30-plus-point outings, and recorded nine double-doubles. He subsequently earned [[NBA Development League Impact Player of the Year Award|NBA D-League Impact Player of the Year]]<ref>{{cite web|url=http://dleague.nba.com/news/ryan-gomes-named-2015-16-nba-d-league-impact-player-year/|title=Ryan Gomes Named 2015-16 NBA D-League Impact Player of the Year|work=NBA.com|date=April 14, 2016|access-date=April 14, 2016}}</ref> and led the D-Fenders to the D-League Finals where they were defeated 2–1 by the [[Sioux Falls Skyforce]]. In 40 games for the D-Fenders, he averaged 18.7 points, 8.2 rebounds and 2.9 assists per game. At the season's end, he was named to the [[All-NBA Development League Team|All-NBA D-League Third Team]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://dleague.nba.com/news/2015-16-all-nba-dleague-teams-release/|title=NBA Development League Announces 2015-16 All-NBA D-League Teams|work=NBA.com|date=April 29, 2016|access-date=April 30, 2016|archive-date=September 4, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160904054918/http://dleague.nba.com/news/2015-16-all-nba-dleague-teams-release/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Coaching career==
On August 23, 2016, Gomes was appointed an assistant coach of the [[Long Island Nets]], a new [[NBA Development League]] franchise.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://longisland.dleague.nba.com/news/long-island-nets-name-gomes-rafferty-assistant-coaches/|title=Long Island Nets Name Gomes, Rafferty Assistant Coaches|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=August 23, 2016|access-date=October 1, 2016|archive-date=August 30, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160830204019/http://longisland.dleague.nba.com/news/long-island-nets-name-gomes-rafferty-assistant-coaches/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

In August 2021, Gomes was named the head coach of Team Overtime, a team that competes in the prep basketball league Overtime Elite (OTE).<ref>{{Cite web|title=Remember Ryan Gomes? He's about to shake up basketball|url=https://www.bostonglobe.com/2021/08/13/metro/remember-ryan-gomes-hes-about-shake-up-basketball/|access-date=January 5, 2022|website=The Boston Globe}}</ref>

In 2023, Gomes joined the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] as an assistant coach. On April 30, 2025, Gomes and the Trail Blazers parted ways.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Blazers Part Ways With Three Assistant Coaches|url=https://www.blazersedge.com/2025/4/30/24421096/roy-rogers-chris-fleming-ryan-gomes-assistant-coach-portland-trail-blazers-chauncey-billups-nba-news|access-date=August 3, 2025|website=blazersedge.com|language=es}}</ref>

On June 3, 2025, Gomes returned to his alma mater, becoming an assistant coach for the [[Providence Friars]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Ryan Gomes Named Men's Basketball Assistant Coach|url=https://friars.com/news/2025/6/2/mens-basketball-ryan-gomes-named-mens-basketball-assistant-coach|access-date=June 3, 2025|website=Friars.com}}</ref>
